whatIs.title: What are Warts?
whatIs.description:
Ever noticed a rough, raised bump on your skin? You might have a wart. Warts are very common, affecting millions of people around Lahore and everywhere else! But don't worry, they're usually harmless.

Here's the breakdown:

points.label: Cause
points.text: Warts are caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV), but don't confuse them with the genital strains of HPV. There are over 100 types of HPV, and some cause these pesky bumps.

points.label: Appearance
points.text: Warts can appear anywhere on your body, but they're most common on your hands (hand warts), feet (plantar warts), and face. They can be rough, smooth, flat, or cauliflower-shaped, and sometimes have tiny black dots in the center.

points.label: Spread
points.text: Warts are contagious, but casual contact isn't usually enough to spread them. The virus thrives in moist environments, so sharing towels or picking at existing warts can increase your risk of contracting common warts.

At Skin Lab Aesthetics, our experienced practitioners use specialized equipment to deliver heat directly to the verruca, destroying the wart cells.
howItWorks: Targeted Heat: The electrical current generates heat that precisely cauterizes (burns) the verruca tissue.
Controlled Depth: Our practitioners carefully control the depth and intensity of the current to effectively remove the verruca while minimizing damage to the surrounding skin on the foot.
benefits: Effective Verruca Removal: Electrocautery is a reliable method for eliminating plantar warts.
Precise Treatment: The electrical current can be precisely directed to the verruca, minimizing damage to surrounding healthy skin on the foot.
Good Option for Thicker Verrucas: It can be particularly effective for thicker, more established verrucas.
considerations: Requires Local Anesthesia: The procedure requires a local anesthetic injection.
Scabbing and Healing Period: There is a healing period involving scabbing, and you may need to take precautions to protect the area.
Potential for Scarring: While generally minimal, there is a slight risk of scarring on the sole of the foot. Our clinicians will take steps to minimize this.
Possibility of Multiple Sessions: Complete removal might require more than one treatment session.

whatIs.title: What is Verrucas (Plantar Warts)?
whatIs.description:
Verrucas are caused by the Human Papilloma virus (HPV), which enters the skin through cuts or abrasions. Certain strains of HPV are responsible for verruca formation, particularly on the soles of the feet. Verrucas are contagious and can spread from person to person through direct contact or indirectly through contaminated surfaces.

Several factors increase the risk of contracting the HPV virus and developing verrucas. These include: walking barefoot in public areas, having a weakened immune system, and prolonged moisture or friction on the skin. By addressing these factors and adopting proper hygiene practices, you can minimize the risk of contracting the HPV virus and developing verrucas.

whatIs.title: What are Moles?
whatIs.description:
Moles, medically known as nevi, are common skin growths composed of melanocytes, the cells that produce pigment (melanin) in your skin. They can appear anywhere on your body, including your face, scalp, and even under your nails.

Here are some key things to know about moles:

It's important to note that most moles are harmless, but some can be a sign of skin cancer. It's crucial to be aware of the ABCD rule for identifying potentially cancerous moles:

If you notice any changes in a mole, such as size, shape, color, or bleeding, it's important to see a dermatologist for a professional evaluation.

points.label: Appearance
points.text: Moles vary in size, shape, and color. They can be flat, raised, smooth, rough, brown, black, tan, pink, red, or even blue. Some moles may grow hair.

points.label: Development
points.text: Most moles appear in childhood and adolescence, with new ones developing less frequently in adulthood.

points.label: Causes
points.text: The exact cause of moles is unknown, but genetics and sun exposure are believed to play a role.

points.label: Types
points.text: There are different types of moles, including common moles, atypical moles, and congenital nevi (present at birth).

points.label: Asymmetry
points.text: One half of the mole doesn't match the other.

points.label: Border
points.text: The edges are irregular, blurred, or notched.

points.label: Color
points.text: The mole has multiple colors within it, such as brown, black, red, white, or blue.

points.label: Diameter
points.text: The mole is larger than 6 millimeters (about the size of a pencil eraser).

items.title: PUNCH REMOVAL
items.description: Ideal for: Various mole types, including those that are slightly raised, deeper, or have irregular borders. Punch removal is particularly useful when a full-thickness sample is needed for diagnostic purposes. It's also a good option for moles in areas where a larger scar would be undesirable.
howItWorks: A specialized tool, resembling a tiny cookie cutter, is used to punch out a cylindrical section of skin containing the mole. The size of the punch tool is selected based on the size of the mole.

What to Expect: The area will be numbed with local anesthetic before the procedure. You may feel a brief stinging or pressure during the punch. Afterward, the wound is typically closed with a stitch or two, or sometimes left to heal on its own depending on the size. The area will be bandaged.
Aftercare: Keep the area clean and dry. Follow your doctor's instructions on bandage changes and wound care. Stitches are usually removed within 5-14 days.
benefits: Uses electric current (cautery) to precisely remove the mole and stop any bleeding. The heat also helps to sterilize the area. Some practitioners may use radiofrequency ablation instead of electrocautery.
Effective for both moles and warts, as well as other skin lesions.
May require multiple treatment sessions depending on the mole's depth, particularly for deeper moles, to minimize scarring. This allows for controlled, layer-by-layer removal.
Often results in a small, circular scar that may be slightly depressed.
The tissue removed can be sent for pathological examination if needed.

items.title: SHAVE REMOVAL
items.description: Ideal for: Raised moles on the trunk or limbs that are not too deep and are mostly above the skin surface. It's often used for cosmetic removal of benign moles where a full-thickness excision is not necessary.
howItWorks: After numbing the area, the mole is carefully shaved off at or just below the skin surface using a surgical blade or a specialized shave excision instrument.
What to Expect: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia. You may feel some pressure during the shaving process.

Aftercare: Keep the area clean and dry. Apply a thin layer of antibiotic ointment or petroleum jelly to keep the wound moist and prevent infection. Cover with a bandage. Avoid picking at the scab that forms during healing.
benefits: A quick and simple procedure, often completed in a single session.
Minimal downtime – healing typically occurs within 7-10 days.
Leaves a small pink or slightly darker patch that fades over time. The resulting scar is usually flat and subtle, but the final appearance depends on skin type and healing ability.
No stitches are typically required.
considerations: Important Note: Shave removal may not remove the entire mole, particularly if it has deep roots. This means the mole could potentially regrow. It also makes it more difficult to obtain a full sample for pathological examination if there is any concern about malignancy.

items.title: SURGICAL EXCISION
items.description: Ideal for: Larger moles, deeper moles, moles with irregular borders or suspicious features, or moles that require a biopsy for cancer checks. It's also used for moles in cosmetically sensitive areas where the surgeon can carefully plan the incision to minimize scarring.
howItWorks: The area around the mole is numbed with local anesthetic. The surgeon uses a scalpel to cut out the entire mole, along with a small margin of surrounding healthy tissue (called the excision margin). The depth and width of the excision are determined by the mole's size, location, and appearance.

What to Expect: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia. You will feel a pinching or stinging sensation when the anesthetic is injected. You should not feel any pain during the excision. The length of the procedure depends on the size and location of the mole.

Aftercare: Keep the area clean and dry. Follow your doctor's instructions on wound care, including bandage changes and cleaning. Avoid strenuous activity that could stretch the incision site. Stitches are typically removed within 5-14 days. Scarring is inevitable, but the surgeon will use techniques to minimize it. Scar massage and silicone sheeting can further improve the appearance of the scar over time.
benefits: The most comprehensive method for ensuring complete mole removal.
Allows for a biopsy to rule out any cancerous cells. This is crucial for any mole that is changing, bleeding, or has other suspicious characteristics.
Stitches are used to close the wound, promoting proper healing and minimizing scarring. The surgeon will carefully align the skin edges to create the most aesthetically pleasing result possible.
considerations: Important Considerations: Surgical excision usually leaves a linear scar. The size and appearance of the scar will depend on the size and location of the mole, as well as your individual healing response.
